**Organizational Purpose and Mission**


The heart of our program is the **Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA)**, a specially trained and supervised community volunteer, appointed by the dependency court judge. Research shows just 1 consistent, stable, and healthy relationship significantly improves adult outcomes for foster children. For more than 2 decades, our mission has been to advocate for abused and neglected children in the foster system, ensuring their voices are heard and their needs are met through our CASA volunteers. Our vision is to champion without compromise for the best interest of every one of the 300\+ foster children in **Yolo County** by providing each of them with a CASA volunteer. We serve our mission and will achieve our vision through our diverse constituents, whom we call our “Hearts of Yolo.”

**POSITION SUMMARY**


Full\-time **Executive Director (ED)** is **Yolo County CASA’s** chief external officer, chief fundraiser, and public voice. The ED’s primary charge is to grow the organization’s revenue and community presence so every foster child in Yolo County can be matched with a CASA volunteer. The ED spends the substantial majority of their time outside the office: cultivating and soliciting major donors, building foundation and corporate partnerships, strengthening relationships with government agencies and elected officials, and serving as the organization’s chief spokesperson.

  

The ED retains full accountability to the Board of Directors for all organizational outcomes i.e. programmatic, financial, and operational, but does not manage internal day to day operations. Yolo CASA has an experienced Program Director who manages programs, staff supervision, finance and bookkeeping, HR administration, and office operations, and reports directly to the ED. The ED’s internal role is that of leader and chief champion: setting direction, connecting the team’s daily work to the mission and to the donors who fund it, and empowering the Program Director to run the organization. This structure exists deliberately to protect the ED’s external focus; candidates should expect and embrace a role that is predominantly relational, revenue\-oriented, and community\-facing.

 **Key Responsibilities**

**A. Revenue Growth and Fund Development (\~45\-50% of time)**

* Develops and executes a multi\-year fund development plan spanning major gifts, annual giving, foundation and corporate grants, planned giving, and signature events, with annual revenue goals set jointly with the Board.
* Manages a portfolio of major donors and prospects; leads cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of 5/6\-figure gifts.
* Researches, pursues, and secures new funding sources, including foundations, corporations, government funding streams, and individual philanthropy, with an expectation of increasing revenue within the first 18–24 months.
* Oversees the strategy and success of annual fundraising events, including sponsorship solicitation, marketing, and volunteer engagement, with event execution supported by staff.
* Partners with the Board to build a culture of philanthropy, including supporting 100% board giving, equipping board members to open doors and make introductions, and engaging them in cultivation and stewardship.
* Ensures the donor database, gift acknowledgment, and donor communications are accurate, timely, and relationship\-building, with administration supported by staff under the Program Director.

 **B. External and Community Relations (\~20\-25% of time)**

* Serves as chief spokesperson, giving voice to Yolo CASA’s vision with donors, media, community organizations, civic groups, faith communities, and the public.
* Develops and maintains strong working relationships with the dependency court, county agencies, elected officials, California CASA, and community partners.
* Leads marketing, communications, and brand visibility strategy to advance the CASA mission, expand volunteer recruitment pipelines, and grow the donor base.
* Represents Yolo CASA at community events, including occasional evening and weekend engagements, which are a core and expected part of this role.

 **C. Executive Leadership and Board Partnership (\~10\-15% of time)**

* Works with Board to develop, review, and report on strategic goals, revenue goals, and organizational performance; provides regular dashboards on fundraising pipeline, finances, and program outcomes.
* Develops the agency budget in collaboration with the Board Treasurer and Program Director; adheres to the Board\-approved budget and all financial policies adopted by the Board.
* Works with the Board President to support the work of the Board, including meeting planning, member recruitment, and governance policies.
* Keeps the Board informed of trends in child welfare, philanthropy, and the CASA network that affect strategy.

 **D. Organizational Oversight, through the Program Director (\~10\-15% of time)**

* Leads and supports the Program Director while overseeing organizational performance, operations, HR, finance, IT, vendors, and compliance.
* Retains ultimate accountability for program integrity and compliance with Welfare and Institutions Code §100–109, CA Rule of Court 5\.655, and all funder and government requirements, with day\-to\-day management delegated to the Program Director and program staff.
* Fosters a healthy, mission\-driven organizational culture and ensures fair and consistent administration of HR policies through the Program Director.

**Position Overview**


Reporting to the Executive Director, the Managing Director of Marketing \& Communications (MarCom) is a strategic leader who proactively creates and elevates our messaging and communication strategy to raise awareness of our mission, expand our media presence, and deepen connection among key stakeholders. The Managing Director of MarCom will oversee and support the implementation of City Year’s branding strategy in Los Angles to ensure consistent coherent representation of CYLA’s impact across all departments and communication outlets, including CYLA’s social media platforms. As a member of the City Year Los Angeles Senior Leadership Team (SLT), they will be a highly effective storyteller who can bring to life City Year’s impact. They will manage the Sr. Marketing \& Communications Manager.  

  

This position is perfect for someone who is entrepreneurial with proven communications experience, and who is a proactive leader, creative, strategic thinker, and willing to challenge old conventions to push beyond traditional communications.  

  

The ideal candidate cares deeply about addressing systemic inequities in education and can represent CYLA powerfully in community spaces. This individual should be able to operate at a high level, able to think about the big picture and the best way to communicate and engage the community at large.  

  

City Year values and continuously works to build an equitable and inclusive culture where people with diverse lived experiences feel they belong.**Job Description**

**Responsibilities**

**Marketing \& Communications Strategy**

* In partnership with the Executive Director, Board Members, SLT, and the City Year headquarters’ teams, lead the development and implementation of a strategic and diversified Marketing \& Communications plan that meets current goals and anticipates future needs and growth objectives.
* Lead 20th Anniversary Board Committee to create and implement milestone Marketing \& Communication strategy.
* Develop clear communication cascade and strategy for disseminating communications to external audiences (e.g., communication medium, audience, etc.)
* Leverage and amplify the national organizational Marketing, Communications, and Creative teams’ content, strategy, and materials to advance the Los Angeles and organizational impact.
* In collaboration with the Managing Director of Development, create the strategy, messaging, and design of all fundraising communications, including event invitations, sponsorship decks, event programs, donor\-facing videos, and stage remarks.
* In collaboration with the Impact team, analyze ongoing program data to support storytelling of the impact of our work throughout the year.
* Develop and implement strategic initiatives aimed at building awareness of CYLA locally by leveraging LA assets that strengthen the brand.
* Collaborate with Managing Director of Government Relations to position City Year in the community and with public officials to help build awareness of our work and garner support.
* Deepen City Year Los Angeles’ presence and reputation in communities where we serve.

**Senior Leadership \& Staff Management**

* As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, develop Los Angeles site strategic plan and lead implementing the site’s local operating plan.
* Work with SLT and national leaders to understand priorities and business goals and develop strategies to meet the organization’s needs.
* Serve as a strategic advisor to SLT on narrative positioning, reputational considerations, and public\-facing communications including major fundraising moments and campaigns.
* Leverage Board where appropriate to reach departmental and site\-wide marketing \& communication goals.
* Serve as a CYLA representative at local events and community functions.
* Manage the Sr. Marketing \& Communications Manager, building and maintaining a relationship by creating an environment of open and honest two\-way communication.
* Provide both positive and constructive feedback and coaching to support direct report’s development.
* Ensure professional accountability with direct report and team through clear expectations, weekly check\-ins, and formal performance reviews.
* Partner with all City Year Los Angeles departments through site events, projects, and cross\-departmental committees as needed to ensure site\-wide goals are met.

**Marketing Implementation**

* Oversee the development of clear and consistent CYLA branding and messaging for external stakeholders, in line with org\-wide parameters.
* In collaboration with the Sr. Marketing and Communications Manager and a contracted designer, oversee all marketing and branding materials to be used regularly at CYLA events, recruiting efforts, and external communications.
* In collaboration with the Development team, develop a multi\-tiered email drip campaign for new donors, top\-of\-funnel volunteers, and general stakeholders, guiding them through a tailored engagement journey with clear communications and desired outcomes based on audience segmentation.
* Support content development for City Year Los Angeles’ Instagram, Facebook and Twitter accounts, blog, E\-newsletter, eBlasts, and publication of all other electronic communications.
* Ensure consistency of messaging within CYLA by sharing expectations, tone, and content with other departments.

**Content Strategy \& Storytelling**

* Oversee creation of all communications collateral, including multi\-media, videos, website, media materials, and other items as needed.
* Oversee the creation of annual impact reports tailored for individual donors, foundations, program sponsors, and team sponsors to ensure meaningful stewardship and donor recognition.
* Support development and core messaging for all major fundraising initiatives, including the annual Spring Break Gala, ensuring alignment across all communications, collateral, and event deliverables.
* Collaborate on language for donor proposals

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
**Chief Development Officer****About the Client** Our client is a mission\-driven nonprofit focused on civic education and democracy\-building, engaging youth and communities in civic learning nationwide. As the organization scales its impact, they're building out a modern development function to match their ambitions — creating a brand\-new C\-suite role to lead the charge.


**About the Role** This is a newly created, first\-ever Chief Development Officer position, reporting directly to the President \& CEO and overseeing a team of 2 (including a Sr. Director of Advancement). The CDO will own org\-wide development strategy, leading the transformation from a grant\-centered funding model to a diversified, relationship\-driven philanthropy operation spanning major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, alumni engagement, and institutional funding. This is a hands\-on leadership role — the CDO will personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors and close six\- and seven\-figure gifts, while also building the systems, team, and board engagement needed for long\-term fundraising growth.


**Responsibilities**

* Own org\-wide development strategy and drive an initial $600K–$1M in annual contributed revenue, with sustained year\-over\-year growth
* Lead the shift from grant\-centered fundraising to a diversified, relationship\-driven philanthropy model (major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, alumni, institutional)
* Personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors; close six\- and seven\-figure gifts; run moves management and stewardship
* Build alumni\-engagement pathways to convert former program participants into an active donor community
* Lead and mentor the development team; set KPIs, dashboards, and forecasting; ensure disciplined CRM (Salesforce) usage
* Serve as the CEO's fundraising partner and drive board engagement in donor cultivation and solicitation

**Requirements**

* 10\+ years of progressive nonprofit development/fundraising/advancement experience, including ownership of fundraising strategy and revenue growth
* Demonstrated success personally closing multiple six\- and seven\-figure gifts
* 5\+ years supervising development staff
* Proven ability to build a diversified development function beyond grants
* Genuine mission alignment with civic education, democracy, and/or youth civic learning

**Benefits \& Why Join**

* Ground\-floor opportunity to build and define a brand\-new C\-suite function
* Direct partnership with the CEO and board on organizational fundraising strategy
* Hybrid/remote flexibility, with HQ based in Calabasas, CA

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Pauma Economic Development Corporation (PEDC) is the senior executive responsible for the day\-to\-day leadership and long\-term growth of the Corporation's business enterprises on behalf of the Pauma Band of Luiseño Indians. The CEO reports to the PEDC Board of Directors and oversees the Corporation's operating businesses — currently including the Pauma Heritage QuikStop, the Pauma Travel Center Starbucks, and Pauma Tribal Farms — along with finance, human resources, and legal/compliance functions.

The CEO will be accountable for building the internal organization, systems, and financial discipline needed for PEDC to grow into a diversified, sustainable economic engine for the Tribe. This includes strengthening budgeting and reporting processes, improving operating margins across existing businesses, and identifying and vetting new lines of business — including agriculture, retail, hospitality, and government contracting opportunities — that fit the Tribe's assets and long\-term goals.

The CEO must have strong general management experience and the judgment, discipline, and work ethic to help a young, growing tribal enterprise mature into a well\-run, professionally managed organization. Above all, the CEO should be excited about building something from the ground up and dedicated to helping PEDC meet and exceed the goals set by the Board and the Tribe.

**CEO Value: Management and Oversight**

The CEO will demonstrate a track record as a results\-oriented leader skilled in developing relationships, identifying viable business opportunities, and building a small organization's processes and culture. The CEO should have experience growing and professionalizing an organization, ideally in retail, food \& beverage, hospitality, agriculture, or tribal enterprise settings, and be comfortable operating with a lean staff and a hands\-on management style.

The CEO must be a leader who can help the team deliver measurable, cost\-effective results that make the Tribe's economic vision a reality. Importantly, the successful CEO will have the confidence and communication skills to work closely with the Board, tribal leadership, and community members while running day\-to\-day operations.

It is essential that the CEO bring efficient, right\-sized systems that increase productivity without over\-engineering process for an organization of this scale, and that the CEO have prior experience helping a small enterprise grow in a disciplined, sustainable way.

* Creating, communicating, and implementing the Corporation's vision, mission, and overall direction; leading development of the annual budget and business strategy.
* Overseeing the complete operations of the Quik Stop, Starbucks, Tribal Farms, and any future PEDC enterprises in accordance with Board\-approved plans and budgets.
* Directly managing or overseeing finance/bookkeeping, human resources, and legal/compliance functions, and any future direct reports as the organization grows.
* Soliciting advice and guidance, when appropriate, from the Board, and providing the Board with timely, accurate financial and operational reporting.
* Formulating and implementing the strategic plan that guides the direction of the Corporation, including evaluation of new business lines.
* Evaluating the financial and operational success of each business unit and taking corrective action where performance lags budget.
* Maintaining awareness of the competitive landscape, market conditions (fuel, retail, agriculture commodities), and opportunities for expansion.
* Representing the Corporation in tribal, civic, and professional settings at the local, state, and national level.
* Demonstrating the leadership necessary to make the Corporation's mission a success, including attracting and developing future talent as PEDC grows.

**Desired Skills and ExperienceRequired Qualifications**

The CEO has proven experience managing a small\-to\-mid\-size business or business unit, with the operational and financial discipline to help PEDC's enterprises grow profitably.

* Minimum of a BA in business or a related field; MBA preferred but not required.
* Business operations and P\&L responsibility for an organization or business unit generating at least $2–5 million in annual revenue.
* Direct experience in retail, convenience store, food \& beverage, hospitality, or agriculture business operations.
* Experience working within or alongside tribal government or tribal enterprise structures strongly preferred.
* Strong operational experience: ideally 7\+ years in a senior management role, including P\&L accountability.
* Demonstrated success in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, and monitoring systems, with experience overseeing finance, HR, and operations functions.
* Skills in organizational development, personnel management, budgeting, and resource planning; demonstrated ability to build systems from scratch in a small organization.
* Excellent people skills, a results\-focused, bottom\-line orientation, and sound business judgment across analysis, experience, and common sense.
* Exhibits qualities of integrity, credibility, and honesty.
* Flexible and able to multi\-task; comfortable in an ambiguous, resource\-constrained, fast\-moving small\-business environment.
* Strategic vision and agility — able to think strategically about new business lines while managing today's operations.
* Leadership and organization — capacity to manage and lead a small team directly, and to scale the organization thoughtfully as revenue grows.
* Action\-oriented — enjoys hands\-on work, and comfortable being the most senior person handling both strategic and day\-to\-day tasks in a small enterprise.

Overview:
**POSITION SUMMARY**
The Deputy Director of Curatorial Affairs is responsible for the overarching vision and strategy that bring together exhibitions, collection gallery installations, and collection initiatives that support OMCA’s brand as a museum, garden, and gathering place and that advance its social impact of building trust, understanding, and connection between people and communities. Working closely with the Director \& CEO and other department managers, the position leads the development of a comprehensive content calendar for the Museum’s temporary exhibitions and collection installations that showcase the breadth of OMCA’s interdisciplinary collections, center equity and community voice, engage multiple constituencies, and tell the unique and compelling stories of Oakland and California. The position also partners closely with the Senior Director of Learning, Experience and Programming in leading the Content and Experience “circle” that comprises departments that collaborate to create a dynamic and integrated set of exhibitions and programs that align with the Museum’s mission and achieve OMCA’s audience, social impact, and financial sustainability goals. As a member of the Senior Directors Council, the position shares in overall leadership for the Museum, including responsibility for strategic planning and policy\-making. This position oversees approximately 35 employees in the Collections, Curatorial, Design, and Production departments, and directly coaches and supervises 6 positions.  


Responsibilities:
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**
The following reflects OMCA’s definition of essential functions for this position, but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. OMCA may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this position at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons. **INSTITUTIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES*** Support the Museum’s mission, values, vision, and core commitment to the visitor experience, community engagement, and institutional relevancy for the future
* Contribute to and support the OMCA strategic plan, annual priorities, and institutional initiatives
* Contribute to a positive organizational culture based on mutual respect, a spirit of collegiality, cooperation, and an openness to many perspectives
* Participate in a culture of ongoing learning, collaboration, innovation, creativity, and community engagement
* All positions will have core functional responsibilities, cross\-functional team activation and learning and development as a core function of each role.

 **POSITION DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES****Executive Responsibilities*** Provide leadership to the overall institution as a member of the Senior Directors Council, contributing to policy\-making and ensuring the Museum’s vitality and success through active communication, problem\-solving, and decision\-making
* Provide leadership for institutional planning, annual priorities, and institutional initiatives
* Contribute to the prudent and ongoing monitoring of OMCA annual budget and financial demands to ensure a sustainable future
* Demonstrate exceptional leadership skills in motivating staff, delegating tasks, encouraging independent problem\-solving by individuals and teams, and providing an understanding of the institutional vision
* Keep apprised of trends and developments in the museum and non\-profit field and ensure that OMCA maintains leadership as a model for a 21st century museum in service to the public
* Work with specific Board committees as staff liaison as assigned
* Serve as Acting Director in the absence of the Executive Director, as requested
* Serve as a spokesperson for the organization in the community, the field and media; participate in and present at professional conferences and conventions, attend community and civic gatherings on behalf of the organization; and play an active role in sharing OMCA’s work with the field and keeping abreast of developments in the field

 **Leadership and Strategy*** The Deputy Director of Curatorial Affairs oversees the work of the Senior Curator of Art, Senior Curator of History, Curator of Natural Sciences, Design Director, Director of Collections, and Associate Director of Production to:
* Translate OMCA’s strategic plan, social impact, and business model into multi\-year institutional exhibition and core gallery priorities and budgets, monitoring performance and adjusting course to meet targets

SPOKANE ARTS seeks an Executive Director who will be a passionate steward of regional arts leadership. The Executive Director (ED) reports to the chair of the Spokane Arts Governing Board of Directors and meets regularly with the Board and the Spokane Arts Commission. The Executive Director will have overall strategic and operational responsibility for the Spokane Arts’ contract staff, volunteers, programs, partnerships, and execution of its mission. The ED will act as the primary spokesperson for Spokane Arts.

The preferred candidate will be drawn to the mission of Spokane Arts and will possess the following: significant leadership skills with demonstrated success in supervisory and budget management; appreciation for arts \& culture across disciplines; a demonstrated commitment to equity and accessibility; the ability to be a passionate, articulate spokesperson for arts \& culture; fundraising experience, preferably in the arts or nonprofit sector; a self\-motivated style, coupled with a positive attitude and a collaborative spirit; the experience to develop and implement strategic planning for the organization; an action\-oriented, adaptable, and innovative approach to organizational planning.

Since 2017, the organization has contracted with the City of Spokane to manage a portion of the city’s collected admissions tax, 33% of which is dedicated to arts and culture by city ordinance. The admissions tax is a 5% fee charged as part of admission to for\-profit ticketed entertainment like concerts, movies, and more. The 33% of admissions tax dedicated to arts and culture funds the Spokane Arts Grant Awards (SAGA), the only local grant program solely dedicated to arts \& culture, and previously funded various programs including the curation of the Chase Gallery, the city poet laureate program, murals, public performances, a short film documentary series, Queer Art Walk, the annual Arts Awards, and more. **Organizational Purpose and Mission**


The heart of our program is the **Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA)**, a specially trained and supervised community volunteer, appointed by the dependency court judge. Research shows just 1 consistent, stable, and healthy relationship significantly improves adult outcomes for foster children. For more than 2 decades, our mission has been to advocate for abused and neglected children in the foster system, ensuring their voices are heard and their needs are met through our CASA volunteers. Our vision is to champion without compromise for the best interest of every one of the 300\+ foster children in **Yolo County** by providing each of them with a CASA volunteer. We serve our mission and will achieve our vision through our diverse constituents, whom we call our “Hearts of Yolo.”

**POSITION SUMMARY**


Full\-time **Executive Director (ED)** is **Yolo County CASA’s** chief external officer, chief fundraiser, and public voice. The ED’s primary charge is to grow the organization’s revenue and community presence so every foster child in Yolo County can be matched with a CASA volunteer. The ED spends the substantial majority of their time outside the office: cultivating and soliciting major donors, building foundation and corporate partnerships, strengthening relationships with government agencies and elected officials, and serving as the organization’s chief spokesperson.

  

The ED retains full accountability to the Board of Directors for all organizational outcomes i.e. programmatic, financial, and operational, but does not manage internal day to day operations. Yolo CASA has an experienced Program Director who manages programs, staff supervision, finance and bookkeeping, HR administration, and office operations, and reports directly to the ED. The ED’s internal role is that of leader and chief champion: setting direction, connecting the team’s daily work to the mission and to the donors who fund it, and empowering the Program Director to run the organization. This structure exists deliberately to protect the ED’s external focus; candidates should expect and embrace a role that is predominantly relational, revenue\-oriented, and community\-facing.

**Team**: Higher Education\- North Carolina

**Location**: In\-Person in either Fayetteville or Raleigh, NC

**Employment** **Type**: Temporary, Full\-time

**FLSA Classification**: Exempt

**Start Date**: January 5, 2027


About Braven
Braven is a national nonprofit that prepares promising college students to secure a strong first opportunity after college graduation through a career\-accelerating program.


We work with higher education and employer partners to offer a life\-changing experience that begins with a semester\-long course for college students, followed by support that lasts through graduation.


Together, our ambition is to help rebuild the middle class and revitalize the American Dream.


To learn more, take a look at Braven’s Jobs.


About the Role
In order to achieve its ambition of serving 80,000\-100,000 Fellows over the next decade, Braven is hiring an Executive Director (ED) in North Carolina (NC). This person will lead our efforts to launch and oversee Braven’s potential new NC region, including its first potential new higher education partner within NC. The ED will also work with the Central External Affairs team and the future NC External Affairs Director to raise roughly $9M for the first three years of programming before the launch of the new school site, among other external priorities.


Should a partnership with a higher education institution in the NC solidify, this temporary position would become a permanent full\-time regional role, leading the NC team as the region’s most senior\-level executive and the face of Braven. They will be responsible for all major outcomes in the region and set the vision and direction for how Braven comes alive successfully in their region. They build and lead the regional program team and a regional advisory board, guide expansion decisions alongside their regional board, manage their External Affairs Director and lead their External Affairs strategy in close collaboration with the central External Affairs team, serve as a Braven organizational leader on the Alignment Team (AT) and ensure they and Braven are the primary thought leaders in the college\-to\-career space in their region.


The ED will initially report to the Chief of Regional Success and Innovation and ultimately transition to report to the Founder \& CEO and be part of Braven’s Alignment Team (AT), the organization’s leadership body.

* Implementing a comprehensive multi\-year strategic plan to reach our vision for scale and excellent outcomes with our prospective partner and future NC region, higher education partners.
* With the Regional Senior Director, ensuring strong program execution resulting in both positive experiences and outcomes for Fellows, volunteers, and partners
* Building, managing, and expanding a regional advisory board that will help maximize the NC region’s impact, narrative, and sustainability

**Stakeholder Management and Awareness Building (30%)**

* Ensuring the health of key stakeholder relationships at both university and employer partners, including university and corporate executives
* Raising Braven’s brand awareness through thought\-leadership, awards, public speaking, social media, and press pieces
* Explore the local political landscape and engage in critical policy efforts when relevant

**Regional Fundraising and Sustainability (30%)**

* Raising roughly $9M prior to the launch of the new school, among other external priorities.
* Deepening our political capital and thought leadership to ensure that our region maintains its meaningful position in the educational fabric of the community
* Focusing on significantly growing and diversifying a sustainable funding base that will include gifts from individuals, corporations, foundations, and government

**Team Leadership and Management (20%)**

* Attracting, hiring, and developing a team of diverse and talented staff members
* Directly manage and develop the Regional Senior Director and Director, External Affairs
* Coaching and developing regional staff members to exhibit strong cultural leadership skills and orientations
* Serving as the model and leader of Braven culture within the hub
* Serving on the organization’s Alignment Team to influence organization\-wide impact, growth, and sustainability

  

**Requirements**  

  

Minimum Requirements* BS/BA
* 7\-10 years leadership experience as an Executive, leading a department, or similar, with a verifiable track record of achieving successful outcomes while maintaining an inclusive, equitable, and sustainable team culture.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 1\-3 years in non\-profit, higher education, economic or workforce development, or a chamber of commerce
* Proficiency in Google Suite, Slack, Asana, Salesforce, Jira, Confluence
* You have a demonstrated commitment to and understanding of the experiences of first\-generation college students and students from low income backgrounds.
* You exemplify Braven’s core values
* Your experiences have informed your belief in Braven’s mission and have prepared you to work with or for Braven’s student Fellow population

* Experience building and working in partnership with partner organizations, funders, a Board of Directors, and other key constituents
* Strong presence, communication skills, relationship\-building skills, and maturity that engender respect and facilitate a strong partnership with very senior\-level staff and Faculty, high\-profile community stakeholders and civic leaders, Braven staff, Fellows, and Leadership Coaches
* High level of personal responsibility, professional maturity and humility, commitment to personal growth, and self\-awareness of one’s own leadership style and its impact on ot

Our client is the **fastest\-growing commercial entrance, door, loading dock, and access control company in the industry**. As the company rapidly expands its footprint across New England, they are seeking a high\-impact **Regional Director of Operations** to serve as the tactical right\-hand leader to the **Chief Operating Officer** (a 25\+ year industry turnaround executive) while working closely alongside the **Chief Executive Officer** (former President of ASSA ABLOY Entrance Systems).

This is not a theoretical desk job or a slide\-deck role. This is a **boots\-on\-the\-ground, roll\-up\-your\-sleeves operational leadership position** for a field\-tested leader who loves being on jobsites, integrating newly acquired businesses, standardizing service delivery, and driving profitable P\&L growth across regional branches.

The primary objective of the Director of Development is to develop long\-term relationships with alumni, donors and prospects, built on a firm understanding of donors’ interests, passions and values, to cultivate, solicit and close five\-, six\- and seven\-figure gifts.
